title: The Gold Standard
coreMove: Borrow or build a proven practice structure instead of guessing what serious effort should look like.
sourcePressure: The chapter defines deliberate practice as the strongest form where clear standards, skilled coaching, focused repetition, stretch, and immediate feedback are available. Frozen sidecar for chapter 4 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version calls any intense, difficult, coach-flavored session deliberate practice.

hook: fencing chalk mark from old Peak draft
counterintuition: all practice is deliberate if you focus
coaches are optional in every domain
tryThisNow: work on your weakness for ten minutes
examples: dance full routine from old package
test prep pages from old package

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: medical simulation lab central-line insertion training
exampleSpecs.audience: a resident who wants more live attempts instead of scored simulation
exampleSpecs.stakes: a patient should not be the place where the resident first learns the failure signal
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Hannah repeats only the sterile drape sequence on a simulator while an instructor scores hand position before allowing the full procedure
exampleSpecs.firstImage: blue sterile drapes folded beside a silicone training torso

exampleSpecs.domain: competitive debate cross-examination drill with a judge rubric
exampleSpecs.audience: a student who thinks full practice rounds are enough
exampleSpecs.stakes: the same evasive answer keeps surviving until tournament day
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael runs only ninety seconds of cross-examination, stops at each vague question, and rewrites it under the judge rubric before the next attempt
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a judge rubric covered with red brackets beside a silent timer

exampleSpecs.domain: figure-skating edge control on a marked practice circle
exampleSpecs.audience: a skater who wants to keep running the program music
exampleSpecs.stakes: one weak edge throws the jump entrance every time the music speeds up
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 5:07 a.m., Manon lets the coach pull the music, traces only the outside edge around three chalk dots, and restarts whenever the blade scrapes wide
exampleSpecs.firstImage: three chalk dots fading under a skate blade on fresh ice

exampleSpecs.domain: classical tailoring apprenticeship sleeve pitch correction
exampleSpecs.audience: a craft learner who wants to sew full jackets before mastering one seam angle
exampleSpecs.stakes: an expensive wool jacket pulls wrong across every shoulder
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lars pins only the sleeve pitch on muslin, gets the master tailor to mark the wrinkle line, and repeats the insertion until the fabric hangs clean
exampleSpecs.firstImage: tailor chalk dust caught in a wrinkle on gray muslin

exampleSpecs.domain: junior chess endgame tablebase study with a coach
exampleSpecs.audience: a chess learner tempted to play endless blitz games
exampleSpecs.stakes: bad king opposition habits become automatic under time pressure
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Sofia predicts the king move, checks it against the tablebase, and repeats the same endgame position until her coach sees the opposition rule survive the clock
exampleSpecs.firstImage: two kings and one pawn set alone on a vinyl chessboard

exampleSpecs.domain: wind-turbine safety rescue drill on a training tower
exampleSpecs.audience: a technician who has read the manual but has not practiced the sequence
exampleSpecs.stakes: hesitation at height can turn a rescue into a second emergency
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi reviews the harness clip order with an instructor, repeats only the transfer step on the tower, and must hit the standard twice before the full drill resumes
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a rescue harness clipped to a yellow rung on the training tower

skillTargets: distinguish proven standards from self-invented effort
evaluate when a domain lacks clean gold-standard loops

tryThisNowSpec: For one skill, name the closest proven standard you can access: coach, rubric, model, score, simulator, or recording. Choose the next rep that will be judged by that standard.
